payload.claim: `cut_off` is decided by substring-matching the literal text `"error_max_turns"` against the pre-formatted `endings` strings, which only fires when the attempt's `subtype` was exactly `error_max_turns`. The codebase's own canonical predicate for this exact signal, `cut_off_at_turn_ceiling` in `saffron/cell/session.py` (lines 366-385), checks `terminal_reason == "max_turns" or subtype == "error_max_turns"` and documents why both are needed: a result event can carry one field without the other, so keying on subtype alone silently misses a cutoff whose ending would render as e.g. `"IMPLEMENTING error (max_turns)"` — text that does not contain the substring `error_max_turns` at all. Because `history`'s whole purpose (item 123) is to stop a past cell's true ceiling-need from being read as merely 'used' the way SA-0031 and SA-0087 were missed by eye, silently mislabeling a terminal_reason-only cutoff as 'used' instead of 'a floor' reproduces the same class of miss this change exists to fix, and the new tests only exercise the subtype-literal case (`cutoff.endings = ["IMPLEMENTING error_max_turns"]`), so nothing here would catch it.
